name: Acromesomelic Dysplasia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Acromesomelic Dysplasia

criteria.description: Presence of disproportionate short stature with shortening of middle and distal segments of limbs
Characteristic radiographic abnormalities including hypoplasia of the ulna and fibula, and shortening of metacarpals and metatarsals
Identification of pathogenic variants in the NPR2 gene or other associated genes
Mild facial dysmorphism such as midface hypoplasia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of disproportionate acromesomelic short stature with characteristic radiological findings; genetic confirmation supports diagnosis but is not mandatory
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is recommended for confirmation and differentiation from other skeletal dysplasias

pathognomonic.symptomName: Disproportionate shortening of middle and distal limb segments
searchTerms: short middle and end limb segments
disproportionate shortening of forearms and lower legs

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hypoplasia of ulna and fibula bones
searchTerms: small forearm and lower leg bones
small bones in palms and soles
mild flatness of cheeks and nose

occasional.symptomName: Mild facial dysmorphism beyond midface hypoplasia

rare.symptomName: Respiratory complications due to thoracic cage abnormalities
searchTerms: lung issues due to rib cage

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms secondary to spinal abnormalities
searchTerms: nerve or brain symptoms from spine issues
neurological problems caused by spinal abnormalities

imaging: Radiographs showing shortening and hypoplasia of ulna and fibula
Shortened metacarpals and metatarsals on hand and foot X-rays
Delayed bone age on skeletal survey
genetic: Mutations in GDF5 or BMPR1B genes in some subtypes
other: Clinical assessment of disproportionate limb shortening
Family history may be positive for autosomal recessive inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Characteristic facial features including frontal bossing and midface hypoplasia
Milder short stature with less pronounced limb shortening
FGFR3 gene mutations distinct from achondroplasia
Predominant shortening of metacarpals and metatarsals without limb shortening

redFlags: Severe disproportionate limb shortening at birth
Progressive respiratory distress due to thoracic cage abnormalities
Neurological deficits suggestive of spinal cord compression
references: Maroteaux P, Le Merrer M. Acromesomelic dysplasia: clinical and radiological features. J Med Genet. 1989.
